Secretary, DoLR Reviews Implementation of WDC-PMKSY 2.0 and World Bank-Assisted REWARD Programme in Odisha
articles.full_content:
Appreciates 89% financial expenditure under WDC-PMKSY 2.0; directs authorities to expedite 7 slow-moving projects and complete all projects by 31.3.2027. Advised to complete all planned REWARD activities ahead of the March 31, 2027 closure date
​Shri Dilip Kumar, Secretary, Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, visited Odisha to review the progress and ground-level implementation of the Watershed Development Component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 2.0 (WDC-PMKSY 2.0) and the World Bank-assisted Rejuvenating Watersheds for Agricultural Resilience through Innovative Development (REWARD) programme.
​Field Visit and Community Interaction
During the field visit, Shri Dilip Kumar inspected various watershed development interventions in the WDC-PMKSY 2.0 project area in Tangi Block of Khordha District. He appreciated the quality of execution on the ground, particularly noting the active involvement of local communities, Water Users' Groups, and Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
​Interacting directly with beneficiaries and user group members, the Secretary assessed the socio-economic and ecological impact of the interventions and discussed the role of local institutions in ensuring the long-term sustainability of the created assets. He also appreciated Odisha’s community-centric approach to watershed development, emphasizing that people’s participation is critical for effective natural resource management, enhancing farmers' livelihoods, and building climate-resilient rural communities.
​Review of WDC-PMKSY 2.0 Progress
Reviewing the State's overall performance under WDC-PMKSY 2.0, the Secretary appreciated Odisha’s achievement of approximately 89% financial expenditure, with 38 out of 60 sanctioned projects currently at the completion stage.
​However, expressing concern over the relatively slow pace in 7 projects where financial expenditure remains below 60%, Shri Dilip Kumar directed the concerned authorities to intensify field monitoring, initiate immediate corrective measures, and expedite pending works to ensure all projects are completed within the stipulated timeline.
​“Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” Campaign
As part of his visit, the Secretary planted a sapling under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” campaign, reinforcing the Government of India’s commitment to environmental conservation and ecological sustainability.
​Review of World Bank-Assisted REWARD Programme
Following the field inspection, the Secretary, along with the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), held a detailed review meeting on the World Bank-supported REWARD programme. Underscoring the importance of adhering to project milestones, the Secretary instructed the implementing agencies to accelerate execution and ensure the completion of all planned activities well before the programme closure date of 31st March 2027.
​During the visit, the Secretary was accompanied by Dr. C. P. Reddy, Senior Additional Commissioner

Second Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 concludes at Agra, Emphasising Sustainability, Community Ownership and Gram Panchayat-led Water Governance
articles.full_content:
Senior Officials Visit Water Supply Infrastructure and Participate In Jal Arpan Diwas Celebrations Across Five Villages in Uttar Pradesh Participating States/UTs reaffirm their commitment towards accelerating implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
The second regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, organised by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, concluded today at Agra, Uttar Pradesh. The conference brought together representatives of seven northern States and Union Territories to deliberate on key strategies for accelerating implementation, strengthening sustainability and ensuring long-term functionality of rural drinking water supply systems
As part of the two-day regional conference, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti , today visited rural drinking water supply infrastructure and participated in the Jal Arpan Diwas celebration at Badhera (Bhadaira) W/S Scheme and 456 MLD WTP, Etah.
In the valedictory session, Secretary, DDWS emphasised that the Regional Conference had provided an important platform for States/UT to develop a common understanding of the reforms envisaged under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and to learn from one another's experiences. Referring to the field visits undertaken during the day, he highlighted innovative practices observed in Uttar Pradesh, including the use of solar energy for rural water supply schemes and command-and-control systems for monitoring and operation of water supply infrastructure, and encouraged States to examine such practices for wider replication.
Highlighting that rural drinking water service delivery is fundamentally a local service, Shri Meena stressed the importance of strengthening ownership of water supply assets by Gram Panchayats and local communities. He noted that Jal Arpan represents an important step towards transferring responsibility and ownership of drinking water infrastructure to communities and underscored the need to build the financial, technical and institutional capacities of Gram Panchayats for sustained service delivery.
He said that infrastructure creation must be complemented by effective management, regular water quality surveillance and community participation. He reiterated the need for convergence among Departments of Panchayati Raj, Rural Development, Skill Development and Drinking Water to strengthen operation and maintenance, build local capacities and promote source sustainability through initiatives such as Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari. He called upon States to move towards sustainable, community-owned and efficiently managed rural drinking water systems while strengthening Gram Panchayats as the foundation of Viksit Villages and Viksit Bharat.
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM called for digital mapping of all drinking water supply infrastructure and highlighted the importance of leveraging existing institutional platforms

MoU between MoSPI and Ashoka University to Strengthen Academic and Institutional collaboration
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and Ashoka University signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi on 27th November 2026. The occasion was graced by Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Shri Purnendu Kishore Banerjee, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI; Dr. Prachi Mishra, Dean, Ashoka University; and senior officers of the Ministry. Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division, MoSPI, and Shri Sachin Sharma, Registrar, Ashoka University signed the MoU. Ms. Reena Singh, DDG, NSSTA while moderating, emphasised that this collaboration would serve as foundation in bringing together two institutions sharing a common interest in advancing knowledge and strengthening institutional capacities for evidence based policy making.
Dr. Saurabh Garg, in his address, emphasised the importance of developing an overarching framework for collaboration in communicating research, in addition to initiatives on training and applied research and build a coherent, integrated approach to data management and governance. He stressed the importance of fostering synergies between government institutions and academic organisations to leverage expertise promote innovation and strengthen the country's statistical ecosystem.
The MoU envisages collaboration across a range of areas, including faculty exchange, exposure visits, collaborative research, sharing of academic resources and publications, organising joint seminars, conferences and workshops, customised short-term academic programme, etc. These initiatives are expected to facilitate mutual exchange of knowledge, expertise and ideas in emerging areas of statistics and data governance, while encouraging research and the development and adoption of innovative statistical methodologies.
The MoU marks yet another step towards fostering stronger institutional linkages between statistical agencies and academic institutions in the endeavour to build a robust, responsive, innovative and future-ready National Statistical System.
articles.summary: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) and Ashoka University signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi on 27th November 2026. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Shri Purnendu Kishore Banerjee, Director General (Data Governance), MoSPI; Dr. Prachi Mishra, Dean, Ashoka University; and senior officers of the Ministry.

Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman concludes extensive pre-budget consultations for Union Budget 2027-28
articles.full_content:
More than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the pre-budget consultations
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired a series of pre-budget consultation meetings for the preparation of the Union Budget 2027-28 between 16 and 26 November 2026 .
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 13th and final Pre-Budget Consultation with Yuva for the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi, today.
More than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the consultations. These included industry associations, domain experts, leaders of India Inc, academics, youth representatives and practitioners from Agriculture and Rural Development; Manufacturing; MSMEs and Startups; Capital Markets and Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI); Information Technology; Infrastructure, Energy and Sustainability; Employment and Labour; Housing, Urbanisation and Culture; Health and Social Issues; Research & Development and Higher Education; School Education, Vocational Education, Skilling and Sports; Youth Affairs; and Economics. The consultation meeting with youth representatives was a novel initiative this year.
Ms. Anuradha Thakur , Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran , Chief Economic Adviser; senior officials of the Ministry of Finance; and Secretaries of Ministries and Departments concerned also participated in the discussions.
The consultations generated a wide range of forward-looking recommendations aimed at strengthening India's human capital, innovation ecosystem, manufacturing competitiveness, agricultural productivity, housing security, and educational outcomes. Stakeholders emphasized the need for reforms that can further accelerate economic growth while ensuring broad-based and inclusive development.
Among the key suggestions received were measures to promote the domestic manufacturing of biofertilisers and advanced biotechnology-based agricultural inputs; initiatives to enhance India's competitiveness in Artificial Intelligence through the development of sector-specific AI models optimised for locally available hardware; programmes to strengthen cyber-hygiene awareness among MSMEs and smaller financial institutions; and targeted interventions to support rural youth and workers in transitioning to productive non-farm employment and sustainable enterprises.
Participants also recommended launching a nationwide reading movement to ensure that every child can read and comprehend a newspaper by the end of Grade 5. In the housing sector, stakeholders highlighted the importance of promoting rental housing as a significant avenue for expanding affordable housing in urban areas. Suggestions were also made to accelerate the development of Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities to support young Indians as they transition from education to employment and to entrepreneurship.

MoSPI launches State Dashboard on eSankhyiki to improve access to State-level statistics
articles.full_content:
Effective dissemination of official statistics requires that users can readily find the data they need, access them in usable formats and reuse them for analysis. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) developed eSankhyiki as a one-stop window for official statistics. The portal enables users to search datasets, explore indicators through interactive visualisations, and consult the accompanying metadata. Users can access data through direct downloads in machine-readable formats and through Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), which allow data to be retrieved and used in other applications. Currently, the eSankhyiki portal hosts 43 statistical products with 1109 datasets comprising more than 139 million records.
The Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR) places emphasis on strengthening subnational statistics and expanding the use of digital tools across statistical processes, including dissemination. Through its Support for Statistical Strengthening component, the scheme seeks to strengthen the capacity of States and Union Territories to produce more granular statistics, including at the district level, and support their use in local planning and policymaking.
In keeping with this emphasis on subnational statistics and digital dissemination, MoSPI has launched the State Dashboard on the eSankhyiki portal. The dashboard brings together State-level data for selected indicators already available across statistical products on the portal. It has been developed in collaboration with the Institute for Competitiveness.
The dashboard currently presents 283 indicators of 21 statistical products across 10 broad themes , including agriculture, education, work and wages, and gender and inclusion. Users can select a State and a theme to view the available indicators, or explore a theme across States. Interactive charts and filters support data exploration, while the accompanying metadata and statistical notes provide the context needed to interpret the figures. Users can also download the underlying data and metadata, and download or share visualisations. By bringing together indicators from multiple statistical products into coherent, theme-based State profiles, the State Dashboard strengthens the transition from data availability to effective data utilisation.
Through this initiative, MoSPI reiterates its commitment to strengthening the country's statistical ecosystem by leveraging technology and innovation to make official statistics more accessible, transparent, interoperable and useful for informed decision-making. The dashboard will be expanded progressively and additional indicators will be added. This forms part of the ongoing effort of MoSPI to improve access to subnational statistics for policy, planning and research.
The State Dashboard will be accessible through the eSankhyiki portal at https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in

PIB’s ‘Varta’ Programme Held at Khumulwng; Focus on Awareness about Drug-Free India, Census and Waste Management
articles.full_content:
Agartala, 26 November 2026: The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Agartala Branch, today organised a discussion-based ‘Varta’ programme at Khumulwng, focusing on building a drug-free India, ensuring public participation in the Census and promoting proper waste management. Speakers highlighted the important role of the media and journalists in creating awareness about these three key issues.
The programme was held at the Office of the Chief Officer, Agriculture Department, Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC). Runeil Debbarma, Chief Executive Member of TTAADC, attended as the Chief Guest. Jitendra Debbarma, Member of the District Council, and Ranjit Debbarma, Editor of ‘Chini Khorang’ and Secretary of Khumulwng Press Club, were present as Guests of Honour. Bishu Karmakar, Member-Secretary of the Tripura State Pollution Control Board, and Debashish Lodh, retired Assistant Director of the Department of Information and Cultural Affairs, participated as expert speakers.
Runeil Debbarma thanked PIB for organising the programme and stressed the need to raise awareness at every level of society for its overall progress. He said public awareness and participation are essential not only for building a drug-free society but also for proper waste management and the successful conduct of the Census.
Ranjit Debbarma highlighted the importance of the Nasha Mukt Bharat campaign and said that creating awareness is crucial to achieving its goal. He also underlined the important role of journalists in spreading awareness among people through the media.
Bishu Karmakar spoke in detail about waste management. He said improper waste management can damage drainage systems and harm the ecosystem of water bodies, directly and indirectly affecting public health. He also noted that waste is now increasingly being viewed as a resource. According to him, around 1.6 to 1.7 lakh tonnes of waste are generated in the country every day. He explained the four categories of waste that need to be segregated— wet waste, dry waste, sanitary waste and special care waste. He also discussed the new rules related to waste management. Highlighting the role of journalists in bringing cases of improper waste management to the notice of the concerned departments, he said that every urban local body in Tripura has a waste management system in place.
Debashish Lodh described the Nasha Mukt Bharat campaign as a social mass movement and said that it cannot be successful overnight. Everyone must come forward to build a drug-free society, and journalists have a responsibility to raise public awareness in this regard. He observed that everyone is a soldier in the mission to build a drug-free India.
Speaking on the Census, Debashish Lodh said that the country's development plans and future policies depend on accurate Census data. People's participation is essential for comprehensive planning. However, many people either provide incorrect information or withhold details during the Ce
